req.title: Update form GET returns 200 for author
req.statement: The system shall serve the update form at GET /<id>/update when the current user is the post's author.
triggers: update form get returns 200 for author

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /<id>/update must return HTTP 200 when the current user is the post's author. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — authenticated author requests their own post's update form and receives 200; (2) negative — unauthenticated user requests the update form and receives a redirect (302) not 200, confirming login_required guard; (3) boundary — authenticated non-author requests another user's post update form and receives 403, confirming author-check logic. Each test uses exact status code assertions to kill comparison-operator and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_update_form_get_200_for_author
preconditions: Database seeded with user id=1 (username=test, password=test)

expected: Response body contains update form content
trace: R-FLASKR-039: system shall serve update form at GET /<id>/update when current user is the post's author
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_get_200_for_author():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_resp = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_resp.status_code == 302
    resp = client.get('/1/update')
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert b'update' in resp.data.lower() or b'Edit' in resp.data or b'title' in resp.data.lower()

test_update_form_get_200_for_author()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_get_redirects_unauthenticated_user():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    resp = client.get('/1/update')
    assert resp.status_code == 302
    assert resp.status_code != 200
    location = resp.headers.get('Location', '')

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_get_state_transition_login_then_access():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    pre_login = client.get('/1/update')
    assert pre_login.status_code == 302
    assert '/auth/login' in pre_login.headers.get('Location', '')
    login_resp = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_resp.status_code == 302
    post_login = client.get('/1/update')
    assert post_login.status_code == 200
